item.title: Nadi edge Malolo 33–31 in Round 9 thriller
item.description: Nadi secured a hard-fought 33–31 win over defending Skipper Cup champions Malolo in Round 9, with the Under-20 side also winning 34–32. Nadi skipper Peni Naruma says the team is proud of the performance after holding firm for the full 80 minutes.
item.content:encoded:
Nadi secured a hard-fought 33–31 win over defending Skipper Cup champions Malolo in Round 9, with the Under-20 side also winning 34–32.

Nadi skipper Peni Naruma says the team is proud of the performance after holding firm for the full 80 minutes.

He says the main objective was to win after Nadi’s loss in round 8 to Nadroga.

Naruma says the team had a strong preparation week and worked hard to correct the errors from their previous game.

He has also praised the coaching panel for working tirelessly with the players throughout the week.

Naruma says Malolo was a tough opponent, especially as the defending Skipper Cup champions.

He thanked the Nadi fans who came out in numbers to support the team, as well as the Vanua o Nadi and Na Momo Na Tui Lawa for their continued support.

Naruma says the win is for the Nadi fans, and the team will now celebrate before preparing for Saturday’s match against Naitasiri at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori.

The Fiji Rugby competitions will return to action on Saturday, 3 October, with Round 10 fixtures scheduled across the country in both the Skipper Tuna Fiji Rugby Provincial Cup and the Subrails Fiji Rugby Marama Championship.

In the Skipper Tuna Provincial Cup, Tailevu will host Malolo at Nakelo District School, while Naitasiri takes on Nadi at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori.

Elsewhere, Taveuni will meet Suva at Wairiki School Grounds, while Rewa faces Nadroga at Burebasaga School Grounds.

In the West, Lautoka will play Namosi at Churchill Park Ground 3, while Ba hosts Kadavu at 4R Electrical Goving Park.

All six Provincial Cup fixtures are scheduled for 1pm for the Under-20 matches and 3pm for the senior matches.

Meanwhile, the Subrails Fiji Rugby Marama Championship will also feature six Round 10 matches.

Tailevu faces Namosi at Nakelo District School, Naitasiri meets Nadi at Ratu Cakobau Park, and Macuata hosts Suva at Subrail Park in Labasa.

Rewa will take on Nadroga at Burebasaga School Grounds, Lautoka meets Namosi at Churchill Park Ground 3, while Ba faces Kadavu at 4R Electrical Goving Park.

The Marama Championship fixtures are scheduled for 11am, except for Macuata–Suva at 12pm and Ba–Kadavu at 1pm.

The Round 10 programme will see provincial teams across the country continue their campaigns as the competition moves further into the season.

item.title: Former Fiji 7s Winger Waisale Beci dies after short illness
item.description: 39-year-old Waisale Beci, a former Fiji 7s winger, has died after suffering from a short illness. Beci was part of the Fiji 7s setup during the 2009–2010 period and emerged as one of the exciting wingers in the national side.
item.content:encoded:
39-year-old Waisale Beci, a former Fiji 7s winger, has died after suffering from a short illness.

Beci was part of the Fiji 7s setup during the 2009–2010 period and emerged as one of the exciting wingers in the national side.

He made his mark during the World Rugby Sevens Series, including Fiji’s successful campaign in Wellington in 2010 under coach Iliesa Tanivula.

World Rugby later described him as a new Fijian star in the sevens game.

He was also named in Fiji’s squad for the 2008–09 season and was involved with the national setup during a period when Fiji remained one of the leading teams in international sevens rugby.

In 2010, Beci scored two tries for Fiji in their opening pool match at the Hong Kong Sevens, as Fiji defeated Thailand 82–7.

His rugby career later continued through involvement in developing young players.

News of Beci’s passing has brought back memories of his contribution to Fiji rugby and his time as part of the national 7s setup.

item.title: Fiji Kulas end MSG campaign with 1-0 win over New Caledonia
item.description: The Fiji Kulas have ended their Women’s MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 campaign on a winning note after securing a 1-0 victory over New Caledonia. The victory is Fiji’s first win of the competition and also their first goal after going scoreless in their opening three matches.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Kulas have ended their Women’s MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 campaign on a winning note after securing a 1-0 victory over New Caledonia.

The victory is Fiji’s first win of the competition and also their first goal after going scoreless in their opening three matches.

The Kulas went into their final match already out of contention for a place in the final following three consecutive defeats.

Fiji began the tournament with a 4-0 loss to Papua New Guinea before suffering 1-0 defeats to Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands.

The 1-0 victory over New Caledonia means the Kulas finish their campaign with three points from four matches.

item.title: Fijian duo Bower and Tavatavanawai named in All Blacks Bledisloe Cup squad
item.description: Bower, the experienced Crusaders prop, and Highlanders midfielder Tavatavanawai are among a 34-man squad selected for the trans-Tasman rivalry, providing a strong Fiji connection in the New Zealand camp. Tavatavanawai brings a powerful ball-carrying presence to the midfield, while Bower offers considerable experience in the front row.
item.content:encoded:
Bower, the experienced Crusaders prop, and Highlanders midfielder Tavatavanawai are among a 34-man squad selected for the trans-Tasman rivalry, providing a strong Fiji connection in the New Zealand camp.

Tavatavanawai brings a powerful ball-carrying presence to the midfield, while Bower offers considerable experience in the front row.

The pair will now have the opportu nity to feature in one of international rugby' s most fiercely contested rivalries.

Codie Taylor will lead the All Blacks into the opening Test at Eden Park on 10th October before the series moves to Sydney for the second Test on 17th October.

The squad also includes a mixture of established All Blacks and emerging talent.

Richie Mo'unga returns at first five-eighth, while Scott Barrett is back from injury and Shannon Frizell returns to the squad after his spell in Japan.

Hookers Codie Taylor (capt), Asafo Aumua, Samisoni Taukei'aho will form the front row with p rops, Ethan de Groot, George Bower, Xavier Numia, Tyrel Lomax, Fletcher Newell and Pasilio Tosi.

item.title: Taveuni focused on improving ahead of Suva clash
item.description: Taveuni rugby player Inoke Ravuiwasa is grateful to God following their hard-fought 17-14 win over Lautoka last Saturday, but says there are still many areas the team needs to improve before their next game. Ravuiwasa says the team had to fight hard and hold on during the final 10 minutes of the match to secure the win.
item.content:encoded:
Taveuni rugby player Inoke Ravuiwasa is grateful to God following their hard-fought 17-14 win over Lautoka last Saturday, but says there are still many areas the team needs to improve before their next game.

Ravuiwasa says the team had to fight hard and hold on during the final 10 minutes of the match to secure the win.

He says Taveuni has faced many challenges this season, but the players have continued to strive and push forward.

Ravuiwasa says they secured the victory because the players believed in the system and trusted their teammates on the field.

Taveuni has recorded three wins, five losses and one draw this season, with their victories coming against Lautoka, Ba and Nadroga.

Taveuni will now turn its attention to Suva, which it will host at Wairiki School Grounds this Saturday.

item.title: Infantino makes bigger cash pledge to FIFA members
item.description: Gianni Infantino has indicated a greater amount of money could be distributed to FIFA members from its estimated FJ$13.1 billion cash reserves. In a letter seen by BBC Sport, and sent to the governing body's six continental confederations on Monday, FIFA president Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered".
item.content:encoded:
Gianni Infantino has indicated a greater amount of money could be distributed to FIFA members from its estimated FJ$13.1 billion cash reserves.

In a letter seen by BBC Sport, and sent to the governing body's six continental confederations on Monday, FIFA president Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which proposed selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, sparking a major backlash.

His letter comes after UEFA and CONCACAF - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America and the Caribbean - demanded FICA pays FJ$22.4 million to all 211 members from its reserves.

The proposal will be considered by the FIFA Council when they meet on 16th October.
